findings.problem: This copy is for accounting firms, but the 'What this can look like for you' list still has the bullets for small business owners (line 18) and finance managers (line 20). Only the firm's own bullet was personalised, so the list speaks to readers who aren't getting this email.
findings.fix: Delete the small business bullet (line 18) and the finance manager bullet (line 20). Keep only the accounting firm bullet, either as a single bullet or as a short sentence.

findings.problem: This copy is for finance managers, but the 'What this can look like for you' list still has the bullets for small business owners (line 18) and accounting firms (line 19). Only the finance manager bullet was personalised.
findings.fix: Delete lines 18 and 19 and keep only the finance manager bullet (line 20).

findings.problem: This copy is for small business owners, but the 'What this can look like for you' list still has the bullets for accounting firms (line 19) and finance managers (line 20). Only the small business bullet was personalised.
findings.fix: Delete lines 19 and 20 and keep only the small business bullet (line 18).

findings.problem: The question 'Does this replace our accountant or bookkeeper?' doesn't fit an accounting firm, because the reader is the accountant. It reads like the generic copy was left in place.
findings.fix: Change the question to suit a firm, for example: 'Does this replace the accountants on our team?' Then answer: 'No. It takes repetitive matching, like checking each client's bank lines against their ledger, off your staff's desks, so they can spend more time on review and judgment.'

findings.problem: 'which can make your accountant's review easier' is wrong for an accounting firm, because the firm does the accountant's review.
findings.fix: Change it to: 'We help keep each client's records tidy and traceable, which can make your team's review easier.'

findings.problem: The sentence uses 'off' twice ('ticking off each card payment ... off their desk'), so it's hard to follow. That goes against the plain English, short-sentence rule.
findings.fix: Split it into two sentences: 'No. It takes repetitive matching off their desk, like checking each card payment against your records. That gives them more time for review and judgment.'
